# @elata-biosciences/app-payments — context for tools and agents

## Role
In-app purchases for apps running inside the Elata App Store's sandboxed iframe. The app asks the parent frame to open checkout and reads what the user owns, over `postMessage`. The store owns checkout, payment verification, and the session; the app never touches wallets or payment details.

## API
- `getCatalog(opts?) -> Promise<CatalogItem[]>`: `{ contentId, title, description?, imageUrl?, priceUsdc }`. `priceUsdc` is USDC base units (6 decimals): "50000" is $0.05.
- `getOwnedItems(opts?) -> Promise<number[]>`: owned contentIds.
- `hasItem(contentId, opts?) -> Promise<boolean>`.
- `requestPurchase({ contentId, priceUsdc?, title?, description?, timeoutMs? }) -> Promise<PurchaseResult>`: `{ status: "success", requestId, txHash } | { status: "cancelled", requestId } | { status: "error", requestId, error }`. `priceUsdc` here is a display hint only.
- Errors: `AppPaymentsError` with `code` in `invalid_input | no_window | no_parent | no_crypto | timeout | not_authenticated | fetch_failed`.

## Correct pattern
1. On startup: `getCatalog()` + `getOwnedItems()`, re-apply benefits for owned items.
2. Render owned vs buyable.
3. `requestPurchase`, then branch on `result.status`. On success, apply the benefit.

## Gotchas
- Branch on `status`, never on `txHash`: an already-owned item returns `{ status: "success", txHash: "" }`.
- Items are one-time unlocks. No consumables, no recurring billing (use an app subscription plan for that).
- Outside the store (localhost) nothing answers: calls time out or reject with `no_parent`. Use a short `timeoutMs` and degrade gracefully.
- Timeouts: `requestPurchase` 5 minutes; queries 10 seconds.
- Item catalogs are configured by the Elata team.

## Message types (wrapped by this package)
`elata:iap:request` → `elata:iap:result`; `elata:iap:getCatalog`, `elata:iap:hasItem`, `elata:iap:listOwned` → `…:result`.

## Docs
https://docs.elata.bio/apps/platform/in-app-purchases
